detailed_rationale:
Bajaj Electricals operates in consumer appliances (fans, small kitchen appliances, and premium brands Morphy Richards and Nirlep) and lighting solutions/EPC. FY26 was a weak year on both growth and profitability: consolidated revenue fell 7.6% YoY to Rs 4,462.16 crore, and the company swung to a full-year consolidated net loss of Rs 90.86 crore versus a profit of Rs 133.42 crore in FY25. Q4 FY26 alone posted a consolidated net loss of Rs 67.5 crore, with EBITDA down 28.9% YoY and EBITDA margin narrowing to 6.1% from 8.4%. Importantly, the Q4 loss was flagged as including exceptional items -- labour-code provisions, a goodwill impairment, and mould-related write-downs -- so the headline loss overstates the run-rate decline versus a clean EBITDA comparison; but even excluding that, EBITDA margin genuinely contracted, so this is not purely a one-off-driven headline. Segment-wise, the core consumer-products business declined 6.86% YoY in Q4, while lighting solutions grew 15.57% -- the smaller, faster-growing segment is not yet large enough to offset weakness in the core appliances business.

The quant scorecard shows low leverage (debt/equity 0.0997x, interest coverage 2.46x) -- this is not a balance-sheet-risk story -- but revenue_cagr_3y (-3.0%) and revenue_growth_1y (-7.6%) confirm a genuine multi-year growth problem in the core business, likely reflecting competitive intensity from both organized peers and unorganized/online sellers in fans and small appliances.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score is Sell on both horizons (23.48 / 24.09) with a balance-sheet flag of AMBER. The balance sheet itself is not the concern (low leverage, adequate interest cover); the concern is a genuine, multi-year revenue decline in the core consumer-products business that has now turned into a full-year net loss, with only partial mitigation from one-off items. That does not support a rescue.
summary: Bajaj Electricals makes consumer appliances (including Morphy Richards and Nirlep brands) and lighting/EPC solutions. The company had a difficult FY26 -- revenue declined and it swung to a full-year loss, driven partly by one-off charges (labour-code provisions, an impairment, and inventory-mould write-downs) but also by genuine, ongoing pressure on margins and volumes in its core appliances business. The lighting segment is growing, but it is not yet big enough to offset the weakness elsewhere.
positive_para: Leverage is low (debt/equity under 0.1x) and interest coverage is adequate, so this is not a balance-sheet-risk situation, and the lighting-solutions segment grew a healthy 15.57% YoY in Q4, showing that not every part of the portfolio is under pressure. Some of the FY26 loss reflects one-off items (labour-code provisions, impairment, mould write-downs) that should not recur every year, which flatters the underlying run-rate relative to the reported headline loss.
negative_para: Even adjusting for one-off items, EBITDA margin genuinely contracted (8.4% to 6.1% YoY in Q4), and the core consumer-products business -- the majority of revenue -- declined for a second straight year (revenue_cagr_3y -3.0%, FY26 revenue -7.6%). Competitive intensity in fans and small appliances, from both organized peers and unorganized/online sellers, appears to be a structural pressure on this business rather than a one-quarter event.
reverse_dcf_judgment: With the company loss-making on a full-year basis, there is no clean trailing-earnings multiple to apply a growth expectation against; the market is implicitly pricing a recovery back toward FY25-level profitability. Given a multi-year revenue decline in the core appliances business and a genuine (not purely one-off-driven) margin contraction, I do not see clear evidence that recovery is underway yet -- this reads as a turnaround call the numbers have not validated.
